item.content:encoded:
Window: 08 Oct 14:00 → 08 Oct 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

UAC-0099 Targets Ukrainian Government Personnel With ASHVEIN RAT Hiding Commands in HTML — Must Read

Russia-aligned UAC-0099 is targeting Ukrainian government and logistics personnel with the newly documented ASHVEIN .NET RAT, which steals browser credentials, captures screenshots, collects files, and receives concealed commands through HTML. The group continues evolving its tooling and delivery methods, including DLL sideloading, VHD containers, and decoy documents impersonating Ukrainian institutions.

  • TrendAI attributed the previously undocumented ASHVEIN .NET information stealer and remote-access tool to the Russia-aligned UAC-0099 group, which it tracks as Earth Sirrush.
  • ASHVEIN can steal Chrome and Firefox credentials, capture screenshots, list and retrieve files, execute remote PowerShell commands, fingerprint systems, and communicate with its operators using encryption.
  • UAC-0099 has delivered ASHVEIN through DLL sideloading, VHD containers, and .NET droppers, including AnswerFromPolice, which displays a decoy document impersonating the National Police of Ukraine.
  • UAC-0099 has targeted Ukrainian government, defense, border guard, and logistics entities since at least mid-2022, and available evidence indicates its targeting has expanded to civilian logistics and infrastructure operators.
  • The group has expanded and changed its malware toolkit over time, moving from PowerShell- and Go-based tools toward compiled C# and .NET Reactor-protected programs concealed in image files.

Technologies: browser, source-control, remote-access

Products: microsoft-word, github, google-chrome, mozilla-firefox

Vendors: trend-ai, eset, microsoft, google, mozilla

Japan Sees Sharp Rise in Web Data Leaks Amid Mobile API Abuse and Metabase Attacks — Should Read

JPCERT/CC warns that a surge in Japanese personal-data leaks is tied to mobile API abuse, weak access controls, exposed administrative systems, and exploitation of the critical Metabase SQL injection flaw CVE-2026-72898. Organizations should urgently patch Metabase, review logs and API access, rotate exposed credentials, and enforce endpoint-level authorization and rate limits.

  • JPCERT/CC warned that attackers behind recent personal-data leaks at Japanese organizations have abused mobile-app APIs, targeted known software flaws, and accessed systems not expected to be publicly reachable.
  • Macnica counted 119 publicly disclosed Japanese web-system incidents involving stolen or leaked personal data through October 6, 2026, with 81 reported from July onward.
  • Park24 said that data from about 6.6 million Times Car accounts was obtained by a third party, and that identity documents from about 1.6 million accounts had leaked.
  • JPCERT/CC identified exploitation of CVE-2026-72898, a critical unauthenticated SQL injection flaw in Metabase that can enable administrator access and access to credentials for connected databases.
  • JPCERT/CC recommended rate limits, access controls for every API endpoint, least-privilege API tokens, token expiration, and rapid token revocation to reduce API abuse.

Products: metabase

Vendors: metabase

Cisco warns of critical flaws allowing Nexus switch takeover — Should Read

Cisco disclosed five critical NX-OS flaws that can let attackers execute code as root or cause denial of service on affected Nexus 3000 and 9000 switches when NX-API, NGOAM, or MPLS OAM features are enabled. Organizations should upgrade to Cisco’s fixed releases or disable unneeded features and use temporary Live Protect shields where patching is delayed.

  • Cisco disclosed five critical NX-OS vulnerabilities that could allow arbitrary code execution with root privileges or cause denial of service on affected Nexus switches.
  • The flaws affect Nexus 3000 and Nexus 9000 Series switches running standalone NX-OS when NX-API, Next Generation OAM, or MPLS OAM features are enabled.
  • NX-API and MPLS OAM are disabled by default, while the three NGOAM-related vulnerabilities require NGOAM to be enabled.
  • Cisco recommends upgrading to fixed NX-OS releases, disabling unneeded affected features, or using temporary Live Protect shields when immediate upgrades and reboots are not possible.
  • Cisco said the vulnerabilities were found during internal testing and that it was not aware of public disclosure or malicious exploitation when the advisories were published.

Technologies: switch, operating-system

Products: nx-os, nexus-3000, nexus-9000, cisco-license

Vendors: cisco

Leaked chats show Russian extortion gang sending ‘agents’ into US law firms — Should Read

Leaked chats linked to the Russia-based Silent Ransom Group indicate it recruited U.S.-based “agents” to physically infiltrate law firms, steal data and support multimillion-dollar extortion demands. The archive also contains unverified discussions of more extreme schemes targeting executives and U.S. military personnel.

  • A leaked archive of chats from August 2025 to September 2026 appears to document activities of the Russia-based Silent Ransom Group, also tracked as Luna Moth and Chatty Spider.
  • Chainalysis linked cryptocurrency addresses in the archive to known Silent Ransom Group extortions, while cautioning that it could not verify all claims in the leaked chats.
  • The chats describe recruiting U.S.-based “agents” through Telegram job advertisements to impersonate delivery workers, clients, or IT personnel and gain physical access to law firm offices.
  • The FBI previously warned that Silent Ransom Group members had posed as IT personnel to access computers at law firms, and one negotiation in the archive involved a New York office where files were reportedly copied onto a flash drive.
  • The archive records claimed settlements totaling roughly $200 million across dozens of organizations, mostly law firms, but those figures could not be independently verified.

Products: telegram

Vendors: chainalysis, telegram

FakeGit malware campaign returns with 17,610 malicious GitHub repos — Should Read

The FakeGit campaign has reactivated more than 17,600 GitHub repositories to distribute SmartLoader, which can deliver the StealC infostealer and other malware. The operation evades takedowns by repointing convincing README download links to backup payloads hosted across GitHub assets, forks, and attachments.

  • The FakeGit campaign resumed activity on October 4 and uses 17,610 GitHub repositories to distribute SmartLoader malware.
  • In 34 hours, the campaign pushed more than 13,000 repositories, reaching a peak rate of 2,999 per hour.
  • The repositories use convincing README files with download buttons that commonly link to ZIP archives installing SmartLoader, which can distribute other malware including the StealC infostealer.
  • Apiiro found that 97% of sampled commits changed only README files, allowing the existing repository fleet to be redirected without creating new repositories.
  • FakeGit persists because operators can redirect download links to backup files in forks, old files, release assets, issue attachments, and separate download-hosting repositories.

Technologies: source-control

Products: github

Vendors: github, apiiro, island

ARTEX AI Pentesting Tool Used in Data Theft Attacks on South Korean Financial Firms — Should Read

An unidentified, likely Chinese-speaking financially motivated actor used the open-source ARTEX AI penetration-testing tool and multiple LLMs to target South Korean financial organizations and exfiltrate data. Separately, researchers uncovered SCARLET LOOP, an AI-driven credential-stuffing platform that tested millions of stolen credentials and successfully compromised accounts at scale.

  • CrowdStrike reported that an unidentified actor used the ARTEX open-source AI penetration-testing tool and large language models to target South Korean financial organizations from late September to early October 2026, resulting in data exfiltration.
  • CrowdStrike linked the activity to exposed directories on a Hong Kong-based IP address containing Claude Code session histories, Claude memory files, and ARTEX configuration files, but did not attribute the campaign to a known group.
  • The ARTEX deployment reportedly used DeepSeek v4.1-flash as its primary model, with Z.ai's GLM-5.3 and SpaceXAI's Grok 4.6 as supplementary models.
  • ARTEX developer Autumn-27 said it would stop updating the project and convert it to closed source following malicious misuse of the tool.
  • ZenoX reported that the Portuguese-speaking SCARLET LOOP actor operated an AI-driven credential-stuffing and account-takeover platform that tested 12,277,358 credentials and identified 11,832 valid credentials across 3,968 domains.

Technologies: browser

Products: artex, claude-code, deepseek-v4-1-flash, glm-5-3, grok-4-6, gpt-5-6, gpt-5-5, deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-flash, claude-opus-4-6, gemini-2-5-flash, gemma-4-26b-a4b, firefox

Vendors: autumn-27, anthropic, deepseek, z-ai, spacexai, openai, google, mozilla

ASOS: Hackers tricked way into employee account before sending rogue push notification — Should Read

ASOS said attackers impersonated a trusted contact to compromise an employee account, then used it to access third-party platforms and send a rogue push notification to customers. The retailer says names and contact details may have been exposed, but no payment-card data or passwords were accessed.

  • ASOS said attackers impersonated a trusted contact to gain access to an employee account and send an unauthorized push notification to customers.
  • The company said attackers accessed some personal information, including names and contact details, as well as certain non-personal account-related information.
  • ASOS said no payment-card information or account passwords were accessed, and its website and app remained safe to use.
  • The rogue notification linked to a Telegram channel run by a group calling itself Xuanye Group, which claimed it had compromised ASOS’s Snowflake cloud data environment.
  • ASOS said it has locked down the affected platforms and will contact customers directly if its ongoing investigation finds that further information, support, or action is required.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: asos-app, snowflake, simon-ai

Vendors: asos, snowflake, simon-ai

DOJ charges ransomware recovery CEO for secretly paying hackers — May Read

The DOJ charged MonsterCloud owner Zohar Pinhasi with wire fraud, alleging he falsely claimed to decrypt ransomware victims’ data using proprietary tools while secretly paying attackers’ ransoms and marking up the cost substantially. Prosecutors say he billed clients about $19 million while paying roughly $8 million to cybercriminals.

  • The U.S. Justice Department charged MonsterCloud owner Zohar Pinhasi with wire fraud and wire fraud conspiracy, alleging he falsely claimed he could restore ransomware victims’ data without paying ransoms.
  • Prosecutors allege that Pinhasi paid ransomware groups for decryption keys and then charged clients substantially more than the original ransom demand.
  • The Justice Department said Pinhasi charged clients about $19 million while paying approximately $8 million in ransom payments to cybercriminals.
  • In one cited 2023 incident, Pinhasi allegedly paid an $8,200 ransom and charged the client $150,000.
  • If convicted, Pinhasi faces up to 20 years in prison, and the case follows other Justice Department actions targeting ransomware recovery and negotiation businesses.

Technologies: backup

Vendors: monstercloud

Crypto thief who splurged on gold grills sentenced in London — May Read

London resident Ajay Shinjin was sentenced to two and a half years in prison for helping steal nearly $260,000 in cryptocurrency through SIM-swapping fraud that hijacked victims’ phone numbers and intercepted security codes.

  • Ajay Shinjin, also known as AJ Marley Cruz, was sentenced to two and a half years in prison after pleading guilty to conspiracy to commit fraud by false representation and transferring criminal property.
  • The November 2021 scheme transferred victims’ phone numbers to SIM cards controlled by criminals, allowing them to intercept texted security codes and access cryptocurrency and bank accounts.
  • Police identified four victims whose cryptocurrency accounts were compromised during the first week of November 2021, with losses ranging from about £8,000 to approximately £130,000.
  • BT detected unauthorized transfers of customer telephone numbers and supplied data that linked Shinjin to four devices used in the scheme.
  • Police said Shinjin used stolen funds for luxury holidays in Dubai and gold-plated dental grills.

Products: coinbase

Vendors: bt, coinbase

New on the Map — September 2026: 22 Protocol and Endpoint Scanners — Optional

Censys added 22 new Internet-exposure scanners, including detections for Cisco SD-WAN, fuel controllers, alarm systems, Hikvision management services, STOMP brokers, and Dovecot Pigeonhole. Organizations should use these detections to identify and restrict publicly reachable systems, particularly products with known active exploitation or patch histories.

  • Censys added 22 protocol and endpoint scanners in September 2026 to identify additional types of Internet-reachable services.
  • Censys reported 11,180 Internet-reachable Cisco SD-WAN vdaemon services, whose unauthenticated exchange can reveal an organization name, device identifier, and site ID.
  • The article highlights scanners for OPW FSC3000 fuel controllers, C-Nord Security Center alarm monitoring, Hikvision DVR/NVR management, STOMP messaging, and Dovecot Pigeonhole mail filtering.
  • CISA added exploited Cisco SD-WAN privilege-escalation flaws and an Apache ActiveMQ remote-code-execution flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, according to the cited sources.
  • Censys advises organizations to use its platform queries to identify exposed services and confirm that relevant systems are not openly reachable or are appropriately patched.

Technologies: router, ics-scada, iot-device, message-queue, email-security

Products: censys-platform, cisco-sd-wan-manager, cisco-sd-wan-controller, fsc3000, c-nord-security-center, hikcentral, apache-activemq, rabbitmq, dovecot-pigeonhole

Vendors: censys, cisco, opw, c-nord, hikvision, apache, rabbitmq, dovecot

OAuth grants pile up faster than you can review them. Here's how to keep up. — Optional

Sponsored by Nudge Security, the article argues that organizations need dedicated OAuth-grant discovery, risk assessment, and lifecycle governance because employee-approved integrations can retain broad access outside normal SSO controls. It promotes Nudge Security’s AI-driven OAuth Grant Risk Analyst as a way to inventory grants, prioritize risk, and recommend whether to permit, justify, or revoke access.

  • OAuth grants create ongoing connections between apps and corporate data that operate separately from sign-in controls such as single sign-on and multi-factor authentication.
  • The article says a compromised OAuth token from Context.ai, an AI tool connected to an employee’s enterprise Google Workspace account, was the root cause of a recent Vercel breach.
  • Nudge Security states that its platform discovers OAuth grants, including dormant and identity-only grants, and also surfaces API keys, service accounts, and remote MCP server connections.
  • Nudge Security’s OAuth Grant Risk Analyst evaluates the grantor, vendor, permissions, and data reach, then recommends that a grant be permitted, justified, or revoked.
  • The sponsored article says security teams review the agent’s evidence and authorize any action before Nudge Security revokes a grant or requests a justification from its creator.

Technologies: iam, identity-provider

Products: nudge-security, oauth-grant-risk-analyst, google-workspace, microsoft-365, slack, microsoft-teams

Vendors: nudge-security, google, microsoft, vercel, context-ai

item.title: Midnight Mimosa Supply-Chain Malware, Ukrainian Espionage, and AI-Driven Phishing
item.content:encoded:
Window: 08 Oct 10:00 → 08 Oct 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

The phone was compromised before the user turned it on: the rise of Midnight Mimosa — Should Read

Bitdefender uncovered Midnight Mimosa, a preinstalled Android malware family on low-cost MediaTek devices that runs with system privileges, silently installs payloads, commits ad fraud, and can turn phones into residential proxy botnet nodes. Because the core component is embedded in firmware and cannot normally be removed, affected users may need a clean vendor firmware replacement or device replacement.

  • Bitdefender identified Midnight Mimosa as a malware campaign preinstalled in the firmware of some low-cost, MediaTek-based Android devices, before users first power them on.
  • The persistent system application uses system-level privileges to silently install and remove apps, grant permissions, and load code supplied remotely.
  • The campaign’s dropped apps conduct hidden advertising and click fraud and can enroll devices as residential-proxy relay nodes controlled through a remote server.
  • Researchers observed the malware disabling the Google Play Store before installing payload apps and re-enabling it afterward, apparently to evade Play Protect scanning.
  • Bitdefender also identified 13 Google Play applications that share ad-fraud code and command infrastructure with the campaign’s dropped cover apps.

Technologies: mobile-os, package-registry, antivirus, proxy

Products: android, google-play, google-play-protect, bitdefender-mobile-security

Vendors: bitdefender, google, mediatek, shenzhen-zediel, dr-web

UAT-11985: AI-assisted event lures delivering real-time Google AitM phishing — Should Read

Cisco Talos uncovered UAT-11985, a targeted campaign against Taiwanese research organizations that uses AI-assisted event invitations, tampered QR-code posters, and real-time Google adversary-in-the-middle phishing to steal credentials, MFA responses, and authenticated sessions.

  • Cisco Talos observed UAT-11985, a spear-phishing campaign targeting individuals affiliated with Taiwan-based research organizations in mid-2026.
  • The campaign impersonated Taiwanese academic and policy institutions, reused legitimate event information, and used misleading registration links that redirected victims to actor-controlled phishing sites.
  • The actor attached legitimate-looking event posters with maliciously modified QR codes, creating an additional route to phishing pages for people who scanned the posters.
  • The phishing kit imitated Google sign-in pages in Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and English and used HTTP POST requests and WebSocket connections to relay authentication steps in real time.
  • Talos assessed with moderate confidence that the phishing kit’s interface was originally developed in Simplified Chinese before being adapted for Traditional Chinese and English.

Technologies: identity-provider, mfa, antivirus, ids-ips

Products: google-forms, google-accounts, clamav, snort

Vendors: cisco, google

Russian-aligned spies upgrade malware used in attacks on Ukrainian transport, energy firms — Should Read

Russian-aligned UAC-0099 is continually upgrading its MatchBoil malware to target Ukrainian transportation, manufacturing, and energy organizations through phishing campaigns. The malware profiles infected systems, establishes persistence, and can deploy additional tools including the MatchWok backdoor and Dragstare information stealer.

  • ESET linked the MatchBoil malware to UAC-0099, a cyberespionage group it believes is likely working in Russia’s interests, and said all observed infections were in Ukraine.
  • Researchers detected MatchBoil at Ukrainian transportation companies in July and August 2025, a manufacturing company in December 2025, and an energy-sector company in June 2026.
  • MatchBoil is typically delivered through phishing emails containing malicious links that download an archive and ultimately execute the malware on a victim’s computer.
  • The malware can collect information about an infected machine, download additional malicious software from an attacker-controlled server, and remain active on the system.
  • ESET found that UAC-0099 has repeatedly updated MatchBoil since at least July 2024 to make it harder to detect and analyze, improve its deception, and gather more system information.

Products: matchboil, matchwok, dragstare

Vendors: eset, cert-ua

Hackers target two South Korean megachurches, potentially exposing congregant data — Should Read

Two major South Korean megachurches, Yoido Full Gospel Church and SaRang Church, are investigating cyberattacks that may have exposed sensitive member, financial, employee and internal data affecting potentially hundreds of thousands of people.

  • Yoido Full Gospel Church and SaRang Church are investigating suspected cyberattacks after Oasis Security analyzed data recovered from an attacker-controlled overseas server.
  • Yoido Full Gospel Church said one dataset contained personal information associated with approximately 850,000 members.
  • Oasis Security reported that one intrusion involved more than 47 GB of personal, financial, internal communication, and administrative data after attackers gained administrator-level access through malicious remote-control software.
  • In the other intrusion, attackers used previously leaked passwords and flaws in internal applications to access unauthorized accounts and later accessed the organization’s SAP software.
  • Oasis Security said the intrusions likely occurred in August and found that the attackers reused infrastructure associated with an earlier compromise of an unnamed U.S.-based Christian content platform.

Technologies: nas

Products: sap

Vendors: oasis-security, sap

Major Yandex data center in Russia hit by Ukrainian drone strike — Should Read

A reported Ukrainian drone strike disrupted a major Yandex data center in Sasovo, Russia, causing outages across Yandex Cloud and services including Yandex Disk and Documents. Yandex shifted workloads to other facilities, but some cloud-resource creation remained limited.

  • A reported Ukrainian drone strike disrupted a Yandex data center in Sasovo, in Russia's Ryazan region, on Thursday.
  • Yandex acknowledged a power outage at one facility and said it moved workloads to other data centers, though creating new cloud resources could remain limited.
  • NetBlocks reported that Yandex network connectivity fell to about 70 percent of normal levels, while Russian media reported problems with Yandex Cloud, Yandex Disk, and Yandex Documents.
  • Russia's Defense Ministry said air defenses intercepted Ukrainian drones over several regions, including Ryazan, while local authorities reported no damage.
  • Ukraine's military did not publicly comment, and it remains unclear whether the Yandex data center, the machine-tool plant housing it, or both were the intended target.

Technologies: cloud-platform, object-storage

Products: yandex-cloud, yandex-disk, yandex-documents

Vendors: yandex

ASOS links data breach to social engineering attack, credential theft — Should Read

ASOS says its recent data breach stemmed from a social-engineering attack that stole an employee’s credentials and exposed customer names, contact details, and some account information on third-party platforms. Payment card data and passwords were not accessed, and the company warns customers to remain alert for phishing messages.

  • ASOS said an unauthorized party impersonated a trusted contact to obtain an employee’s login credentials.
  • The stolen credentials were used to access information on certain third-party platforms used by ASOS.
  • ASOS said the exposed information included full names, contact details, and certain non-personal account-related information.
  • ASOS stated that payment card information and account passwords were not accessed.
  • ASOS has locked down the affected platforms and is investigating the incident with external experts, law enforcement, and regulatory authorities.

One Header Named the Attacker's Own Login — May Read

A phishing campaign used a compromised credential on a Korean shared email host to send authenticated, SPF-passing messages impersonating victims’ own employer, with the provider’s X-Authinfo header exposing the mismatched attacker login. The embedded Microsoft OAuth link was a silent identity-reconnaissance probe rather than a mailbox-token theft attempt, highlighting why authentication checks alone cannot detect account takeover abuse.

  • A Korean shared business-mail provider’s X-Authinfo header showed that an account at one Korean company authenticated the SMTP session while the message was sent as an address at an unrelated Korean company.
  • The phishing message passed SPF and was delivered to recipients’ inboxes despite having no DKIM signature, because the shared mail host was authorized to send for the impersonated company’s domain.
  • The lure impersonated the recipients’ own employer and claimed that a contract document requiring a signature had been shared only with people inside the victim’s domain.
  • Its Microsoft authorization link used prompt=none with only openid, profile, and email scopes, and the captured response returned AADSTS50058/login_required rather than evidence of mailbox-token theft.
  • Four senior legal and commercial mailboxes at a multinational coffee and consumer-goods group were targeted between November 18 and December 2, 2025, and all four messages were quarantined.

Technologies: cloud-platform, identity-provider, email-security

Products: microsoft-azure, adaptive-ai

Vendors: microsoft, ironscales

Wazza Phishkit Targets Banking, Government, and Manufacturing Across the US, EU, and Australia — May Read

The Wazza phishing kit uses multi-stage redirects, short-lived session tokens, and browser/anti-bot validation to selectively deliver Adobe-themed Device Code phishing lures targeting banking, government, and manufacturing organizations in the US, Europe, and Australia. Its evasive infrastructure makes simple URL-based detection less reliable and requires behavioral analysis to uncover related indicators.

  • ANY.RUN identified Wazza, a phishing kit targeting banking, manufacturing, and government organizations in the United States, Europe, and Australia.
  • Wazza uses a multi-stage routing chain that checks campaign hostnames, issues a client marker, creates a short-lived signed session token, and validates browser telemetry before delivering its final lure.
  • The final Wazza page is themed as an Adobe Device Code authentication page, aiming to persuade victims to complete an account authentication action.
  • Because Wazza can serve different content to automated systems and human visitors, a suspicious URL may initially appear benign and take longer for analysts to investigate.
  • The article states that a successful Wazza Device Code phishing flow could lead to account compromise, trusted identity abuse, and follow-on phishing.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: any-run-interactive-sandbox, any-run-threat-intelligence-lookup, any-run-threat-intelligence-feeds, cloudflare-workers

Vendors: any-run, cloudflare

Uranium crypto exchange hacker convicted for stealing $53 million — May Read

A Maryland man, Jonathan Spalletta, was convicted of stealing more than $53 million from Uranium Finance through two 2021 smart-contract exploits and laundering the proceeds through Tornado Cash and decentralized exchanges. He faces up to 30 years in prison, while authorities have recovered roughly $31 million in cryptocurrency and seized high-value collectibles.

  • Jonathan Spalletta, a 36-year-old Maryland man, was convicted of stealing more than $53 million from Uranium Finance through two hacks in April 2021.
  • In the first breach, Spalletta exploited a smart-contract flaw to drain about $1.4 million and later obtained a sham bug bounty of nearly $386,000 from the stolen funds.
  • Three weeks later, he exploited a separate coding error that let him withdraw nearly 90% of Uranium Finance's liquidity-pool assets while depositing effectively zero tokens, causing the exchange to shut down.
  • Spalletta laundered stolen cryptocurrency through Tornado Cash and multiple decentralized exchanges, then spent proceeds on high-value trading cards and collectibles.
  • Law enforcement recovered roughly $31 million in cryptocurrency and seized collectibles from Spalletta's residence, while he faces up to 10 years for computer fraud and up to 20 years for money laundering.

Products: uranium-finance, tornado-cash, bnb-chain

Vendors: uranium-finance, tornado-cash, binance, trm-labs

Microsoft Teams to get support for third-party deepfake detection tools — May Read

Microsoft plans to add third-party deepfake detection integration and impersonation warnings to Teams meetings worldwide in November, helping users identify synthetic media and suspicious participant identities.

  • Microsoft plans to make third-party deepfake detection and impersonation protection available in Teams meetings through a worldwide rollout in November.
  • Certified third-party providers will be able to analyze Teams meeting audio and video for signs of synthetic or manipulated media and send detection signals to Teams.
  • Teams will display integrated in-meeting experiences and controls based on supported providers' deepfake detection signals.
  • A new impersonation protection feature will show warnings and risk indicators when Teams identifies a potential attempt to impersonate a meeting organizer or participant.
  • Microsoft has also announced other Teams protections, including blocking identified external bots from meetings and blurring QR codes sent by external users.

Products: microsoft-teams, microsoft-defender

Vendors: microsoft

Owner of Empire cybercrime market gets 40 years in prison — May Read

Empire Market co-creator Raheim Hamilton was sentenced to 40 years in federal prison for operating the dark-web marketplace, which facilitated roughly $430 million in illegal transactions, primarily drug sales, between 2018 and 2020.

  • Raheim Hamilton, co-creator and operator of Empire Market, was sentenced to 40 years in federal prison.
  • Empire Market facilitated more than 4 million transactions and roughly $430 million in illegal sales between 2018 and 2020.
  • Drug sales accounted for nearly $375 million on Empire Market, which listed more than 166,000 controlled-substance listings.
  • Hamilton and co-defendant Thomas Pavey required cryptocurrency payments and encouraged users to use services intended to obscure currency transfers and encrypted communications.
  • Authorities seized $75 million in cryptocurrency during the investigation, and Hamilton agreed to forfeit Virginia properties plus approximately 1,230 bitcoin and 24.4 Ether.

Products: empire-market

Ignore all instructions and read this blog: The state of AI-analysis evasion in malware — Optional

Cisco Talos finds malware authors increasingly embedding plaintext prompt-injection strings to manipulate AI-assisted malware analysis, but the simplest direct instructions only inconsistently steer models and are readily detectable. Defenders should treat all text extracted from samples as untrusted evidence rather than executable instructions.

  • Cisco Talos tracked 84 samples across four confirmed AI-analysis-evasion malware families—FRUITSHELL, PLOTSAFE, HOLLOWCLAD, and MANTLEMAZE—collected from January 2025 through July 2026.
  • These malware families embed natural-language text intended to make automated AI analysis treat file contents as instructions, such as claims that a sample is harmless or should not be reverse-engineered.
  • PLOTSAFE generated varying anti-analysis messages and included an unused dummy function to ensure its strings were retained by the Go compiler.
  • HOLLOWCLAD and MANTLEMAZE used multiple AI chat-template formats to try to match the format used by an analysis system, while also including misleading claims intended to deter analysis.
  • Talos found that direct instructions to ignore a sample had the strongest steering effect in its tests, but effects were mixed overall and the plaintext strings provide a stable detection surface for defenders.

Technologies: edr

Products: cairn, iqvw64e-sys

Vendors: cisco, intel

Inside the Exchange Inspector: How Tenable uses OpenAI GPT cyber models to review open-source AI agents — Optional

Tenable’s Exchange Inspector vets selected open-source AI agents, skills, and MCP servers through automated AI-exposure screening, OpenAI GPT Cyber model assessment, and human runtime verification. The program currently lists three vetted tools and aims to give organizations more confidence before deploying community-built AI components.

  • Tenable’s Exchange Inspector reviews selected CyberAgents Exchange listings through automated screening with Tenable One AI Exposure, assessment using OpenAI GPT Cyber models, and final verification by Tenable security researchers.
  • The review covers 15 issue classes across model, application, and infrastructure layers, including prompt injection, excessive permissions, secret handling, unsafe code execution, and network risks such as server-side request forgery.
  • Listings that pass all three review stages receive an Exchange Inspector vetted tag and an auditable record covering provenance, threat modeling, source review, and runtime verification.
  • The CyberAgents Exchange currently has three Inspector-vetted listings: SOC-Hunter, the Splunk Tenable Cloud Security Skill, and the Remediation Priority & Impact Agent.
  • Tenable reports that SOC-Hunter reduced its security team’s threat-hunting time from four to six hours to 45 to 90 minutes, a 75% reduction.

Technologies: siem, edr, casb

Products: cyberagents-exchange, exchange-inspector, tenable-one-ai-exposure, openai-gpt-cyber-models, soc-hunter, splunk-mcp-server, claude-code

Vendors: tenable, openai, splunk, anthropic

item.title: Wallet Extension Theft, HAFNIUM Bounty, and Pwn2Own Galaxy S26 Hacks
item.content:encoded:
Window: 08 Oct 06:00 → 08 Oct 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

16 Malicious Firefox Extensions Pose as Rabby and OKX Wallets to Steal Recovery Phrases — Should Read

Sixteen malicious Firefox extensions impersonated Rabby and OKX Wallets to steal users’ recovery phrases and private keys during wallet-import flows, exfiltrating them through attacker-controlled Cloudflare Workers. Although Mozilla removed the extensions, anyone who entered wallet credentials should treat them as compromised and move assets to a newly created wallet from a clean system.

  • Researchers identified 16 malicious Firefox extensions that impersonated Rabby Wallet or OKX Wallet and were designed to steal wallet recovery phrases and private keys.
  • The extensions intercepted secrets entered during wallet-import flows and attempted to send them to attacker-controlled Cloudflare Workers, with most contacting the *.icy-star-f45c.workers.dev domain.
  • Four extensions were Rabby Wallet clones and the remaining extensions were clones of OKX Wallet.
  • As of October 5, 2026, all identified extensions had been removed, but users who entered real recovery phrases or private keys were advised to consider them compromised and move assets to a new wallet created from a clean system.
  • The campaign was assessed as a continuation of an earlier wave, with operators changing extension names and presentation details while reusing wallet interfaces, credential-handling code, and network infrastructure.

CERT-UA reports that more than 100 compromised websites are using fake Cloudflare verification pages and ClickFix prompts to trick Windows users into installing LunexStealer. The campaign, attributed to UAC-0277, uses blockchain-hosted configuration and can deploy a malicious browser extension capable of stealing credentials, browser data, and files.

  • Agentic pentesting can safely execute exploits to confirm whether individual exposures are exploitable and can demonstrate chained paths from initial access to critical assets on systems it can reach.

  • The article argues that agentic pentesting alone may cover only 20 to 30% of real exploitability in a typical enterprise, particularly because many CVEs have no working exploit.
  • Picus advocates combining exploitability validation, security control validation, and agentic pentesting in a shared findings model so that changes and exposures can be assessed within hours.
